content: 1. The metabolism of timolol ophthalmic may be influenced by hepatic enzyme CYP2D6, potentially altering its levels or effects. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Lorcaserin can increase the levels or effects of tolterodine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Lorcaserin can increase the levels or effects of tramadol by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. This interaction is serious; consider using an alternative therapy. 4. Both tramadol and lorcaserin elevate serotonin levels, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Tranylcypromine and lorcaserin both increase serotonin levels, posing a serious risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Trazodone and lorcaserin both elevate serotonin levels, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Lorcaserin and trifluoperazine have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS). Antipsychotics may also enhance serotonergic effects, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitor for signs of serotonin toxicity (e.g., mental status changes, autonomic instability, neuromuscular hyperactivity) or NMS (e.g., hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, autonomic dysfunction). 8. Lorcaserin can increase the levels or effects of trimipramine by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Lorcaserin can increase the levels or effects of valbenazine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the valbenazine dose based on tolerability if co-administered with a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor. 10. Lorcaserin can increase the levels or effects of venlafaxine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. This interaction is serious; consider using an alternative therapy. Both venlafaxine and lorcaserin elevate serotonin levels, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Vilazodone and lorcaserin both increase serotonin levels, posing a serious risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Lorcaserin increases the levels of vortioxetine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, reduce the vortioxetine dose by 50%. 13. Lorcaserin and ziprasidone have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of NMS. Antipsychotics may also enhance serotonergic effects, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitor for signs of serotonin toxicity or NMS. 14. Zolmitriptan and lorcaserin both increase serotonin levels, posing a serious risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 15. Monitor for serotonin syndrome or NMS-like reactions. Discontinue therapy and any concomitant serotonergic or dopaminergic agents immediately if symptoms arise. 16. Studies suggest a potential risk of regurgitant valvular heart disease, though this is unlikely. Monitor patients with congestive heart failure. 17. Advise patients to exercise caution when operating hazardous machinery. 18. Monitor for worsening depression, suicidal thoughts or behavior, or any unusual changes in mood or behavior. 19. Monitor for hypoglycemia in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. If hypoglycemia occurs during therapy, adjust the antidiabetic drug regimen accordingly. 20. Priapism may occur. Men experiencing erections lasting longer than 4 hours should discontinue therapy immediately and seek emergency medical attention to prevent irreversible damage to erectile tissue. Exercise caution in men with conditions predisposing them to priapism (e.g., sickle cell anemia, multiple myeloma, leukemia) or anatomical penile deformities. 21. Use caution in patients with bradycardia or a history of heart block. 22. Lorcaserin may cause a decrease in white blood cell count and other hematological changes. Consider periodic monitoring of complete blood count (CBC). 23. Lorcaserin moderately elevates prolactin levels. Obtain prolactin levels if symptoms of hyperprolactinemia (e.g., gynecomastia) occur. 24. Lorcaserin may cause pulmonary hypertension, though data are insufficient. 25. Lorcaserin may cause confusion, somnolence, fatigue, and cognitive impairment. Advise caution when operating heavy machinery or performing tasks requiring mental alertness. 26. The use of lorcaserin in patients with severe hepatic impairment has not been studied; use caution. 27. Lorcaserin is not recommended in patients with severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease. Exercise caution in patients with moderate renal impairment. 28. Neutropenia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, anemia, and/or decreases in hematocrit and hemoglobin have been reported. Consider periodic CBC monitoring during use. 29. Lorcaserin is contraindicated during pregnancy, as weight loss offers no benefit to a pregnant woman and may harm the fetus. Limited data on lorcaserin use in pregnant women are insufficient to determine the risk of major congenital malformations or miscarriage. Advise pregnant women of the potential risks to the fetus. 30. Appropriate weight gain based on pre-pregnancy weight is recommended for all pregnant women, including those who are overweight or obese, due to the obligatory weight gain in maternal tissues during pregnancy. In animal studies, maternal exposure to lorcaserin during late pregnancy resulted in lower body weight in offspring, persisting into adulthood. 31. There are no data on the presence of lorcaserin in human milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its effects on milk production. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants, advise women receiving lorcaserin therapy that the product is not recommended while breastfeeding. 32. Lorcaserin is generally acceptable for use in pregnancy when controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk.
